- Overestimate prices in early forecast periods when sentiment is low or neutral (e.g., sentiment < 0.3) — model tends to be overly optimistic.
- Underestimate price spikes when sentiment rises sharply (e.g., sentiment > 0.5) — model fails to capture momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model peaks too early and then corrects, leading to overcorrection in subsequent days.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often forecasts higher prices than true outcome after sustained upward trends, especially when sentiment is high.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment spikes, leading to delayed price adjustments.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate later periods (e.g., 15–30 days) when sentiment is positive, suggesting model overweights short-term momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.00–0.53), model tends to average out, missing directional shifts.
- Avoid extrapolating from recent low sentiment — model often underestimates downside risk when sentiment is weak.
